questions.q: Growing degree days count each day's mean temperature above what threshold, given in degrees Fahrenheit?
questions.exp: Each day of the growing season scores the amount by which its mean temperature exceeds 50°F (10°C), and the season's total sorts regions on the Winkler scale from cool Region I to hot Region V. The Court sets this beside macroclimate, mesoclimate and microclimate as its Certified climate terms.

questions.q: Mendoza lies in a hot, dry rain shadow at about 33 degrees south. Which moderator chiefly keeps its best vineyards cool enough to hold their acidity?
questions.exp: Mendoza's vineyards climb from under 1,000 metres around the city to about 1,500 metres in the Uco Valley, and the height brings cold nights, a wide swing from day to night that keeps acidity and colour in the grapes. No ocean, lake or sea fog reaches the province: the Andes wall it off from the Pacific and leave a desert that lives on irrigation.

questions.q: Which rock underlies the steep terraced slopes of Côte-Rôtie in the northern Rhône?
questions.exp: Côte-Rôtie's terraces are cut into schist, the dark, iron-rich mica schist of the Côte Brune with paler gneiss on the Côte Blonde, while Hermitage and Cornas stand on granite. The Court's Certified soil list asks for these northern Rhône rocks alongside Coonawarra's terra rossa and the Gimblett Gravels.

questions.q: Pinot Gris and Pinot Blanc arose from Pinot Noir by which natural process?
questions.exp: Pinot Gris and Pinot Blanc are colour mutations of Pinot Noir: a bud changed its skin colour and growers propagated the new shoot, so the DNA is almost identical. A crossing joins two varieties of one species, as Pinotage does, and a hybrid joins two species, as Vidal does; the Court asks all three terms.

questions.q: In the vine's yearly cycle, which stage follows directly after flowering?
questions.exp: The Court's cycle runs dormancy, bud break, flowering, fruit set, ripening with véraison and hangtime, maturity, harvest and pruning. At fruit set the fertilised flowers become berries, and cold or wet weather at flowering gives a poor set and a smaller crop.

questions.q: When converting a vineyard yield from metric to standard measures, about how many acres make one hectare?
questions.exp: A hectare is 10,000 square metres, about 2.47 acres, so an acre is about 0.4 hectare. To compare a yield in tons per acre with one in hectolitres per hectare the area must be converted first and the weight of grapes then turned into a volume of wine, which is why the Court asks for the conversion formulas.

questions.q: Ripeness of the skins, seeds and tannins, judged apart from the sugar a refractometer reads in Brix, is called what?
questions.exp: Sugar ripeness is what Brix measures; phenolic ripeness is the maturity of the skins, seeds and stems, when tannins taste soft rather than green. In a hot site sugar can race ahead of the phenolics, and canopy management, crop level and hangtime are the vineyard choices growers use to bring the two into step.
